state: The generated-record contract concatenates inline Choice names and static arm-record field names in written order, with metadata last. Runtime still evaluates each spread expression and may choose a previously defined arm record. Both source names are reserved before signature inspection. The compiler builds nominal shapes before sealing; its normal expression checker uses sealed types. A pre-seal projection could inspect annotations on named values, constructor types, fields, indexes, updates and declared function results only to discover shapes. Full expression and arm/error compatibility checks would remain mandatory afterward. Projection cycles or unavailable evidence would produce diagnostics. Compare that annotation projection against building a provisional complete graph, using the normal checker to derive spread shapes, and rebuilding a final graph; or refactoring the expression checker so its shape-only phase can run before sealing while full semantic checks still occur afterward. Every option must reject unresolved cycles, validate complete expressions, and avoid authored execution/provider calls.

shape.instructions: Which alternative best fits the described type-sealing and runtime-evaluation constraints?

criteria.project: Discover record fields from annotations and separately require complete semantic validation.
criteria.rebuild: Derive fields using a temporary checked graph, discard it, and produce a fresh final type graph.
criteria.refactor: Make a reusable shape-only portion of expression checking available during nominal graph construction.
